summary: Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Kwan earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indology scholar who served as a Sanskrit teacher at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, where he was attested in 1892 and as an adhyāpaka in 1929.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University from circa 1923 to 1924 and subsequently at Harvard University from circa 1925 to 1930.

So Takahashi (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Meijo University, where he was an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori (born 1934) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Kogen Mizuno and Hajime Nakamura, he served as a professor at Josai University (1977) and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji under Kodo Sawaki (1949–1957) as well as under Ekō Hashimoto. He taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, and under Gempo Yamamoto (circa 1931–1961). His students included Robert Baker Aitken and Philip Kapleau.

Sogaku Daiun Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, training under Dokutan Sōsan and other teachers. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Nihon University. He taught Yamada Koun and held a post at Kanagawa University.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994), a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies figure, studied at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Kobo-in (1947), founded Chozen-ji (1972), and was president of Hanazono University (1978–1982).

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at the University of Delhi, University of Cambridge, and under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He founded Rigpa in 1975.
Sohanwela Pemarathana is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the National University of Singapore, where Saranindranath Tagore served as his thesis supervisor (attested 2004).

Soiku Shigematsu (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He held a professorship in English Literature at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and was a professor at Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies figure who taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann. He was an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and served as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).

Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893). He founded Ryōbōkai in 1901 and Ningen Zen Kyodan, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki and Zuigan Goto.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied art at Tokyo University of the Arts and California School of Design, and Zen under Sokatsu Shaku. He founded the Buddhist Society of America in 1930 and taught Alan Watts.

Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) was a scholar of history, philosophy, and sinology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He worked at the SMR Research Department (circa 1908–1923) and held posts at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo.

Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (earning a doctorate in 1944) and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937 and was a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served at Oxford as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies and was attested as a researcher at CNRS in 2019.
Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, trained under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936, and was a member of Servants of the Buddha around 1926.
